narrative:
Your loan application has been denied because the model assessing your creditworthiness determined that you have a 58% chance of being a bad credit risk. In other words, based on the available information, you are more likely than not to struggle with repaying the loan, so approving it would be too risky for the bank.

The three most important reasons for this decision relate to your checking account, your property situation, and your installment burden. The strongest influence came from your checking account status: your account is currently overdrawn (below zero), while most approved applicants have a positive balance or no account at all. This signals immediate financial strain, which heavily pushes the prediction toward bad credit.

Next, your property status was a major factor. You have no registered property or assets such as real estate, a car, or savings from a building society or life insurance. Among approved applicants, only a small minority fall into this category, so the lack of property made the model see you as having little financial cushion to fall back on if difficulties arise.

Interestingly, one factor worked in your favor: your installment rate is relatively low at 2% of disposable income, compared to the average of about 3% among borrowers. This suggests you have some room in your monthly budget to handle payments, which reduced your overall risk score. Unfortunately, the negative signals from your checking account and lack of property outweighed this positive point.

To improve your chances in the future, consider building a more stable financial profile. Try to bring your checking account into positive territory, avoid overdrafts, and save up a small buffer. If possible, acquire or document any assets you may have. Even after improving these areas, wait a few months before reapplying, so your recent history can show positive changes.
